samples.summary: A single failing re-run aborts the rest of the batch, yet the verb still reports success
samples.evidence: `for (const run of (red.length ? red : completed.slice(0, 1))) { await github.rest.actions.reRunWorkflow(...); reran = true; }` sits inside ONE outer try/catch (lines 185-210 in agent-rerun.yml, 141-166 in agent-loop.yml). There is no per-run try/catch, so the first `reRunWorkflow` rejection (403 on a run too old to retry, 422 on a run GitHub refuses to re-run, a transient 5xx/rate-limit) breaks out of the loop and the remaining red runs for the SHA are never re-run. Because `reran` was already set to `true` by the earlier successful iterations, the outcome comment still says "Re-running CI now; the review panel will run again and can promote or fix this PR" (agent-rerun.yml:221) / "Re-running CI now to engage the loop" (agent-loop.yml:170) — exactly the false report this change was written to eliminate, since `ciConclusion` (scripts/agent/checks.mjs:84) needs EVERY run for the SHA green and one still-red run leaves gate 1 unclearable forever. Conversely, if the very first call throws, `reran` stays false and the comment claims "No CI run to re-run" although reds exist. The unit-tested `ciRunsToRerun` cannot cover this because the failure is in the call loop, not the selection rule.

samples.summary: Re-running several CI runs for one SHA can make both the CI-fix arm and the panel's fix job push at once, breaking the documented mutex
samples.evidence: The loop now re-runs every red run for the head SHA, so N CI runs for the SAME commit are in flight simultaneously. `.github/workflows/agent-iterate-ci.yml:55` fires its `contents: write` fixer whenever a CI run for the SHA concludes `failure`, and agent-review-panel.yml's `fix`/promote jobs proceed when their run concludes `success` — the comment in scripts/agent/checks.mjs:141-155 states CI's conclusion is a MUTEX between the two arms and that "For any given CI run exactly one arm still proceeds, which is why no extra `concurrency` group is needed". With multiple parallel runs of one SHA that invariant no longer holds: a flaky suite can leave run A green and run B red, and the two arms live in different concurrency groups (`agent-iterate-<branch>` vs `agent-review-panel-<repo>-<branch>-active`), so both can push commits to the PR branch concurrently. Previously only `workflow_runs[0]` was re-run, so at most one new completion event per verb existed and the mutex held.

samples.summary: `conclusion !== 'success'` selects conclusions a re-run cannot turn green (or cannot re-run at all)
samples.evidence: `const red = completed.filter((r) => r.conclusion !== 'success')` treats `cancelled`, `skipped`, `neutral`, `stale`, `action_required` and `timed_out` identically to `failure`. Two consequences: (a) `reRunWorkflow` can reject some of these (e.g. a run GitHub considers not retryable / too old returns 403-422), and with no per-run try/catch (see the other finding) the rejection kills the whole batch; (b) a conclusion that re-running reproduces deterministically (a `skipped` CI run, a `stale` run) makes the verb re-run CI on every invocation while gate 1 in `ciConclusion` — which requires every run to be exactly `success` — can never clear, so `@claude rerun` reports progress on a PR that is permanently unpromotable. `ciRunDecision`/`agent-iterate-ci.yml` deliberately distinguish `failure` from `cancelled`/`neutral`; this selector does not.

samples.summary: Multiple re-run completions serially cancel each other's review panel, wasting rounds and recording no verdicts
samples.evidence: The panel's workflow-level concurrency group is keyed on head repo + branch + 'active' with `cancel-in-progress: true`. Each re-run now emits its own `completed` event with `run_attempt > 1`, all of which the gate at agent-review-panel.yml:164-169 admits, so re-running k red runs creates up to k panel runs in the same group; each newer completion kills the previous panel MID-REVIEW. The file's own comments note a cancelled panel records no verdicts (the `!cancelled()` reasoning near line 898), so the earlier ~13-minute, ~$12 reviews are discarded and the round accounting sees a cancelled round. Only the last-finishing run's panel survives, and if that run is the red one the promote path never runs even though a green sibling exists.

samples.summary: The all-green fallback silently depends on API ordering that `ciConclusion` deliberately stopped trusting
samples.evidence: `completed.slice(0, 1)` picks "the newest" only because `listWorkflowRuns` happens to return runs in descending `created_at`; the doc block for `ciConclusion` (lines 65-83) explains that this ordering dependence was intentionally removed there because a missing/unparseable stamp makes the order unspecified. Harmless today (any single re-run emits the needed `workflow_run` event) but the function's contract is stated as "the newest" while the code guarantees only "whichever the API listed first".

verdict.reason: The code is present exactly as described. agent-rerun.yml:184-210 wraps the entire re-run loop in a single outer try/catch with no per-iteration handling, and `reran = true` is set inside the loop at line 206. A rejection from `reRunWorkflow` on any iteration aborts the remaining red runs, yet the outcome at lines 220-222 still reports "Re-running CI now; the review panel will run again and can promote or fix this PR" whenever an earlier iteration succeeded; if the first call throws, it instead falsely reports "No CI run to re-run" despite reds existing. agent-loop.yml:140-166,170 is the identical mirror. The consequence is grounded: ciConclusion (scripts/agent/checks.mjs:84-89) requires every run for the SHA to be green, so one un-rerun red run leaves gate 1 unclearable while the comment claims otherwise. No guard makes this unreachable: the catch at line 208 only calls core.warning (non-failing), so the misleading comment at 213-225 and the loop-status note at 260-271 still execute; and the step's `retries: 3` (line 118) uses Octokit's retry plugin, whose default exempt status codes include 403/404/422 — the exact failures described — so it does not cover them. ciRunsToRerun (checks.mjs:121-125) is a pure selection function with no invocation, so unit tests cannot cover a mid-loop rejection. This is error handling that mis-handles a partial failure and leaves state inconsistent for what runs next — squarely in the Correctness lane, reachable on the normal multi-red-run path the change exists to handle, so major/blocking.

verdict.reason: The code is present exactly as described. agent-rerun.yml:199-207 re-runs EVERY red CI run for the head SHA in an unserialized loop (mirroring ciRunsToRerun at checks.mjs:121-125), so multiple CI runs for one commit are in flight at once. checks.mjs:141-155 does assert that CI's conclusion is a MUTEX between the arms and that "no extra concurrency group is needed". The two arms are gated per-run: agent-iterate-ci.yml:52-56 fires its contents:write fixer (perms :24-29, job concurrency group agent-iterate-<branch> at :96-98) on conclusion == 'failure', while agent-review-panel.yml:1638-1641 runs its contents:write fix job (perms :1646, push at :1812-1817) when needs.ci.outputs.conclusion == 'success', where the ci job (:286-337) polls only the single run it rode in on. The panel's concurrency group is agent-review-panel-<repo>-<branch>-active (:115-118), disjoint from the iterate group, so nothing cross-cancels. With N parallel runs of one SHA a divergent (flaky/infra) outcome — one green, one red — lets both arms push to the same branch concurrently, the exact failure the panel header documents from #648. I looked for a guard that would make this unreachable and found none: review-round-guard.mjs has no in-flight/agent:fixing check, and agent-iterate-ci.yml's Attempts guard (:148-234) only counts prior failures and checks the paged latch; it never verifies its run is the latest for the SHA. No not-present, already-guarded, or out-of-scope ground applies (races and concurrent-push/data-loss are squarely in the correctness lane).
